column1: # confinement-classes.tsv (harbor#1441, #555 decision 10 (a)) — every class of Bash call that asks to leave the sandbox, and
# its treatment. `admission-observe-report.sh --confinement` joins the ledger's per-class escape count to this file and
# prints `untreated: N`: the classes with no row here, or a row whose kind is not one of the four. A class is a name in
# HARBOR_ADMISSION_CLASSES (bin/library-admission.sh), set from the first verb of the command by floor_obs_class and written to
# the ledger as `x`; `unclassified` is a record from before that field. The observe-report suite holds this file's class
# set equal to the writer's enum, so a class added there with no row here is red.
# kind  allow     a confinement row that lets the call run confined (a host, a path, a socket)
#       route     a tool or hook that does the work outside the wall, or a note that names the confined way
#       operator  an `!` step or sudo install only the operator can run
#       accepted  counted in the week and left on the open retry (#555 decision 11: a rare tool earns no new row)
# `accepted` is a treatment only for a class the week then measures: it is the retry the 2% line counts.

column3: the note on the call itself says this verb runs confined, so the flag is dropped
github.com and api.github.com are on the host list; gh, git and gcx read the token the access hook mints before the call
workload hosts are the private layer's rows (#555 decision 11); a host that escapes repeatedly in the week earns one
the container runtime socket sits outside the write zone; the call is counted, not opened
a script's class is what it runs; the run is counted and the script that escapes repeatedly is classed by its verb
an interpreter runs anything; it is counted, and a repeated cause earns its own row
a host off the list goes through the open retry (#555 decision 11)
a write outside the zone is the refusal the note names; writes inside it never need the flag
launchctl, sudo, open and the like act on the machine, not the repo; the operator runs them with `!`
a loop or group has no single verb; the first verb inside it cannot be read without a parse
the bus directory is a write row, so `event-bus.sh emit` runs confined
the title is written with the Write tool and applied by the session-title hook, never a shell redirect
a verb the enum does not name is counted; a verb that recurs is added to floor_obs_class with a row
a ledger record from before the class field; it ages out with rotation
